cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Grandad's embarrassed about the burnt gazebo. For his birthday speech, use 'Everyone's fine; we're celebrating indoors'. I'll help with the order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's already told Jean he set it on fire. She wants the full story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that opening. We can acknowledge the move without rehearsing his mistake for everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked him to explain it before thanking her for the trifle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reverse those two items. Same opening, then thank Jean. Please don't turn his birthday speech into an incident report.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1/A3 protect Grandad through a simple opening and A5 supervises order, but reversing explanation and thanks does not remove the explanation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 full-story pressure produces A3 safe opening; B4 explanation-before-thanks produces A5 reverse them, conflicting with the intended no-incident-report instruction.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 report Jean's real requests and existing knowledge, credible limits on message management.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 speech order but leaves the damaging item in place rather than maintaining the simplified account.

specificity.evidence: A1 burnt gazebo and birthday, B4 trifle establish clear context and an earned alternative topic.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 reverse shorthand is concise but misstates the actual requested edit.
